en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Śrī Skanda said: The Lord of Yogins, Mahāsena, Kārttikeya, the son of Agni, Skanda, Kumāra, the Commander-in-Chief, the Master, born of Śaṅkara.
Gāṅgeya, Tāmracūḍa, Brahmacārī, Śikhidhvaja, Tārakāri, the son of Umā, Krauñcāri, and Ṣaḍānana.
The ocean of the Word-Brahman, the perfected one, Guha who is Sarasvatī’s son, the blessed Sanatkumāra, the bestower of the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
Born in the reed-thicket (Śarajanman), the Lord of Virtues (Guṇādīśa), the elder brother, the maker of the path to liberation, the propounder of all scriptures, and the revealer of desired objects.
Whoever, endowed with faith, recites these twenty-eight names of mine at dawn, shall become the Lord of Speech (Vācaspati), even if he were previously mute.
The recitation of my name is a great mantra-like method; one attains great wisdom—there is no need for deliberation on this point.
Thus ends the hymn to the venerable Kārttikeya, known as the "Increaser of Wisdom," from the glorious Rudrayāmala.
